intro: 3.12 greatly simplified generics and type aliases (PEP 695), added itertools.batched and relaxed f-string syntax (PEP 701). This section shows them with a Modbus register read plan and a typed reading object.
example_desc: Reading[T] needs no TypeVar or Generic; latest[T] is a generic function; type Address = int creates a lazily evaluated alias whose target lives in __value__. batched(addrs, 125) splits the addresses by the Modbus limit of 125 registers per read.

case.title: Reading 250 registers at once returns exception code 03
paragraphs: Modbus limits Read Holding Registers to 125 registers per request (many devices allow fewer). A program that asked for 250 got Illegal Data Value. Splitting with batched() by the limit removes the hand-written index arithmetic.
Type parameters let one Reading class represent numeric points and text status points alike, and type checkers can tell that latest(temps) returns Reading[float].
steps: Look up the per-request register limit in the device manual and put it in configuration.
Build the read plan with batched() and merge contiguous addresses to reduce requests.
Annotate data classes with PEP 695 type parameters.
Check with mypy or pyright that generic inference is correct.

updates.text: Python 3.12 now receives security fixes only and is expected to reach end of life in October 2028. Since 3.13, batched() accepts strict=True to raise when the last batch is short.

sources.title: Python Developer's Guide: Status of Python versions

exercises.q: With 260 registers, which batches does batched(addrs, 125) produce?
exercises.a: (0, 125), (125, 125) and (250, 10). The short last batch is still produced; use strict=True (3.13+) to require full batches.

exercises.q: How does type Address = int differ from Address = int?
exercises.a: The first creates a TypeAliasType whose value is evaluated lazily, so it can refer to types defined later, and type checkers know it is an alias. The second is an ordinary assignment: Address simply is int.

exercises.q: What happens if the example's f"{point["name"]}" runs on 3.11?
exercises.a: SyntaxError. Before 3.12 an f-string could not reuse its outer quotes inside the braces; you had to write point['name'].

exercises.q: Does Reading[T] check the type of value at run time?
exercises.a: No. Type parameters are for static checkers only; Reading("SAT", "abc") works at run time. Use a validator such as pydantic, or check in __post_init__, when run-time validation is needed.
